exchanges.text: The idea splits into four parts, from the chips themselves to the power that runs them. I'd stand on accelerator chips, since cloud spending is aimed mostly at them, though no listed company is tied to it yet.

Three listed companies have a sourced connection to accelerator chips: Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom. A packaging supplier came up too, but it is privately held, so it stays a lead. Each connection rests on one source, and none says how much of the company's revenue it is.
Both have a sourced connection to the AI chips data centers buy. The point against is the same for both: the largest cloud buyers also design their own chips.

data-center accelerators stop being the large majority of Nvidia's revenue

thesis.sentence: My theme is AI data-center buildout, through Accelerator chips, built on NVDA, because Nvidia earns most of its revenue from accelerators sold into AI data centers, as its own results show. It's wrong if the largest cloud companies cut or pause their AI data-center spending plans. Time frame: Longterm · about 60 sessions.

exchanges.text: The idea splits into four parts, from the chips themselves to the power that runs them. I'd stand on accelerator chips, since cloud spending is aimed mostly at them, though no listed company is tied to it yet.

Three listed companies have a sourced connection to accelerator chips: Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom. A packaging supplier came up too, but it is privately held, so it stays a lead. Each connection rests on one source, and none says how much of the company's revenue it is.

Nvidia's data-center segment, which sells accelerators and systems to cloud companies, was the large majority of its revenue last quarter, so the AI link carries real weight for the company. The strongest point against is that its largest customers also design their own AI chips.
Wrong if: the largest cloud companies cut or pause their AI data-center spending plans

against.text: Its largest customers also design their own AI chips and use them alongside Nvidia's, which could limit how much of their spending it keeps.

wrongIf.text: the big cloud companies shift more of their AI workloads onto chips they design themselves, away from Nvidia accelerators

options.text: the big cloud companies shift more of their AI workloads onto chips they design themselves, away from Nvidia accelerators
the largest cloud companies cut or pause their AI data-center spending plans
data-center accelerators stop being the large majority of Nvidia's revenue

suggestion.reason: The why rests on spending plans for next year and customer chip choices that play out over a few months.

accepts.say: “the largest cloud companies cut or pause their AI data-center spending plans”

exchanges.text: The idea splits into four parts, from the chips themselves to the power that runs them. I'd stand on accelerator chips, since cloud spending is aimed mostly at them, though no listed company is tied to it yet.

Three listed companies have a sourced connection to accelerator chips: Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom. A packaging supplier came up too, but it is privately held, so it stays a lead. Each connection rests on one source, and none says how much of the company's revenue it is.

Nvidia's data-center segment, which sells accelerators and systems to cloud companies, was the large majority of its revenue last quarter, so the AI link carries real weight for the company. The strongest point against is that its largest customers also design their own AI chips.
Wrong if: the largest cloud companies cut or pause their AI data-center spending plans

exchanges.text: The idea splits into four parts, from the chips themselves to the power that runs them. I'd stand on accelerator chips, since cloud spending is aimed mostly at them, though no listed company is tied to it yet.

Three listed companies have a sourced connection to accelerator chips: Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom. A packaging supplier came up too, but it is privately held, so it stays a lead. Each connection rests on one source, and none says how much of the company's revenue it is.
Both have a sourced connection to the AI chips data centers buy. The point against is the same for both: the largest cloud buyers also design their own chips.

exchanges.text: The idea splits into four parts, from the chips themselves to the power that runs them. I'd stand on accelerator chips, since cloud spending is aimed mostly at them, though no listed company is tied to it yet.

Each of the three has a sourced connection to the AI chips data centers buy. The point against is the same for all three: the largest cloud buyers also design their own chips.
Wrong if: the largest cloud companies cut or pause their AI data-center spending plans
